events.text: Credits are running out, so I can't run the generation. I'll explain that and offer a free manual route instead: a 1080x1920 canvas, the photo scaled to 1080x1080 and centered at y=420, a background copy scaled to 1920x1920 and cropped, then a roughly 40px Gaussian blur on the background. The source already has shoulders cut off at the edges, so fitting the full width keeps everything that's there.

I couldn't make the story yet. Your Magic Hour account doesn't have enough credits, so it turned down the job and nothing was created or charged. I tried the cheapest free-plan image model at the free 640px size, so a smaller setting won't fix it. Once you add credits or they refresh, I can run it again.

You can also do it yourself in a few minutes. This method doesn't crop you at all, so your hair and shoulders stay exactly as they are in the photo:

1. **Make a new canvas** that's 1080 × 1920 pixels (the 9:16 story size).
2. **Add the background:** place a copy of your photo, enlarge it to 1920 × 1920 so it covers the whole canvas, and center it. The sides will hang off the edges, which is fine because this layer gets blurred. Apply a strong blur, around 40–60px.
3. **Add your photo on top:** place the original at 1080 × 1080 so it fills the full width. Center it, about 420px from the top. Don't crop it.
4. **Optional:** darken the blurred layer by about 10–20% so you stand out a bit more.
5. Export as a JPG. Don't add any text.

Canva, CapCut, Snapseed or Photopea (free in a browser) can all do this. Many story apps also have a "fit" option with a blurred background that does it in one tap.

The finished story will show everything in your current photo. Your hair fits easily, and the shoulders reach the left and right edges of the picture just like in the original. The extra blurred space only goes above and below you.

If you'd rather I do it, tell me once you have credits and I'll make it with the blurred background and no text. AI-made versions can sometimes slightly change a face, so the manual method above is the safest way to keep the photo exactly as it is.
